name: sgs/filter-search
title: Filter Search
description: A type-to-find search that narrows a filter's options. Two modes: narrow an existing WooCommerce attribute filter's chips (nest inside a Product Filter (Attribute) block), or render its own searchable, tickable term list for any product taxonomy (brand, category, tag, attribute) so it can stand alone in a filter panel. The search input is auto-shown only once the term count passes the threshold.

text.reason: Paints text inside a live <input> field — background-clip:text gradient rendering on typed/placeholder text is non-standard UX and cross-browser inconsistent, and this is the only row in the colour-conformance TEXT census painting a form control rather than static content. Hover state is unaffected by this exemption (textColourHover is flat-only, not gradient).

root.label: Search box
root._note: Single-element block — render.php renders ONE root <div class="sgs-filter-search"> in either mode (attribute-chips or taxonomy-terms). Margin (a single TIER-of-BOXES envelope attr {desktop,tablet,mobile}, folded 2026-09-11) is the ONLY styling capability declared in supports; padding/gap/width/border/fill/text/position/motion have no supports or attrs on this block (spacing.margin is the sole `sgs` support) — every other layout member is an honest GAP, not an omission.

searchMode.description: Where the search box gets its options from. 'attribute-chips' narrows the chips of an ancestor Product Filter (Attribute) block (legacy/default). 'taxonomy-terms' renders its own searchable, tickable list of a chosen taxonomy's terms — usable standalone anywhere in a filter panel.

taxonomy.description: Taxonomy slug used when searchMode is 'taxonomy-terms' (e.g. product_cat, product_tag, a brand taxonomy, or an attribute taxonomy pa_*). Must be registered against the product post type.

showCounts.description: Show each term's product count next to its name when searchMode is 'taxonomy-terms'.

inputBorderColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the search input's border instead of a flat colour. Non-empty wins over inputBorderColour at render time (D636).

inputBorderColourHoverGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the search input's border on hover instead of a flat colour. Non-empty wins over inputBorderColourHover at render time.
